ludwig-crocius.name: Ludwig Crocius
ludwig-crocius.bio: Bremen Reformed pastor and professor at the Gymnasium Illustre. A Dort delegate for Bremen, he stood for Melanchthonian irenicism and moderate orthodoxy rather than high Calvinist strictness, and his Syntagma sacrae theologiae (1636) is the chief systematic statement of that Bremen school.

louis-le-blanc-de-beaulieu.name: Louis Le Blanc de Beaulieu
louis-le-blanc-de-beaulieu.bio: Reformed professor of theology at the Academy of Sedan. His Theological Theses map Protestant and Roman Catholic positions with unusual clarity and restraint; John Owen praised his moderation on justification. Distinctive for irenic comparison without surrendering Reformed confession.

john-davenant.name: John Davenant
john-davenant.bio: Lady Margaret Professor at Cambridge, later Bishop of Salisbury, and a British delegate at the Synod of Dort. He defended Reformed predestination while arguing a broad sufficiency of Christ's death for all—an English moderate-orthodox line often linked with later hypothetical universalism.

robert-baron.name: Robert Baron
robert-baron.bio: Reformed philosophy professor at St Salvator's College, St Andrews. Philosophia theologiae ancillans treats philosophy as the handmaid of theology: scholastic metaphysics ordered to Reformed doctrinal ends, not free-standing speculation.

josue-de-la-place.name: Josué de la Place (Placeus)
josue-de-la-place.bio: Reformed professor at the Academy of Saumur. Best known for denying the immediate imputation of Adam's first sin, teaching mediate imputation instead—a signature Saumur position contested by stricter Reformed orthodoxy and later condemned in some synodical debates.
